brief: The Nasdaq 100 fell roughly 8% over Thursday and Friday and the S&P 500 is down over 10% from its peak, pushing the VIX to its highest level since the April 2025 tariff shock. Index volatility had stayed low most of 2026 because record-low stock correlation let single-stock moves offset each other and 0DTE option selling let dealers buy dips and sell rallies. That calm is breaking: correlation rose to its highest since March, 0DTE flows are shifting, and AI-trade durability doubts accelerated the day after Anthropic's IPO. BofA's Bowler says idiosyncratic risk has caused rotation rather than rupture, but a broad shock lifting correlation remains a risk, and tech-stock fragility events in 2026 are on track for the second-highest count in 30 years, behind only 2025. One-day dispersion spiked on Nov. 5 and echoed smaller on Friday in Micron and Nvidia. JPMorgan's Kaplan says calm can mask building risk until a shock forces de-leveraging. A hedge fund manager argues the longer fragile conditions persist without a positioning reset, the more violent moves will be, and whether the VIX reverts to the 20s or spikes further depends on whether this is a valuations repricing or the start of a credit event.
